utterances.text: As far as I know, the BH Army 1st Corps did not honour it, and I protested a number of times to General Soubirou. They reported to me that they had implemented it, but I'm sure that they didn't. The Sarajevo-Romanija Corps honoured the agreement to the last letter. If we ever did anything fully and completely, then it was the implementation of your agreement with Akashi that was reached on the 18th of February, 1994. That's the so-called TEZ agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: TEZ?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, TEZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, how was all this received by the soldiers and officers of the SRK? And I'm talking about the obligation that we undertook to deprive ourselves of heavy weaponry.

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reaction was that both you and I were labelled as traitors. Why? And I have to tell you because these are very serious words that I'm uttering today, both for you and for me. The reason was very clear. After so many years of fighting they knew what advantages the BH Army 1st Corps had over the SRK, how many more troops they had. If you compared 350.000, 220.000 Serbs. And what was waiting us in terms of the fire coming from the weaponry with the calibre of less than 12.7-millimetres should the 1st Corps of the BH Army decide to use it against the SRK, it would be very difficult for us to counter that. The only advantage that we had had was taken from us. That is why, although the soldiers understood the essence of the agreement and the need to implement it, the majority of them were nonetheless dissatisfied and unhappy about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if the 1st Corps of the BH Army implemented this agreement and to what extent?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, as I said, regardless of all the pressures --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm talking -- I'm asking you about the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll come to that. So regardless of that we managed to realise that, but according to the information that I have and judging by the activity and the operations that they conducted, most definitely did not implement it because on many occasions when we got this protected area I asked UNPROFOR whether it pertained to the entire Sarajevo and they said: No, no, no, it relates only to the 1st Corps of the BH Army. I don't know what pertained to others, but as for them they did not abide by it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 1D01686.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, in this report, regular combat report, of the 31st of March, 1994, sent to the Main Staff you said at 1735 hours movement of the enemy's self-propelled gun was observed on the Franje Rackog Street near the national museum in Sarajevo. Now, according to the agreement was this self-propelled gun something that was allowed to be within the 20-kilometre exclusion zone?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I already said that all calibres in excess of 20.7 [as interpreted] millimetres were excluded, and this one should not have been there or if it was there it should have been under strict control of UNPROFOR and incapacitated in such a manner that it could not be moved elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 1 it says that from the direction of the mechanical engineering faculty there was a burst of fire from small arms and that your forces did not respond. What did you know about the mechanical engineering faculty and the deployment of forces of the 1st Corps across the Miljacka river?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this faculty and this area crossed the Miljacka is an area where there is -- there are quite a few high-rise buildings, there is also the parliament there and other buildings. Now, speaking only about the mechanical engineering faculty would be unjustifiable because that was an area where the sniper units of the 1st Corps were most extensively deployed and were active targeting Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3433, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D01717.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is dated the 5th of May, 1994, and this is all happening after the agreement had been concluded; correct?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have page 2 and then we'll come back to page 1. Page 2 in both versions, please. Maybe even page 3 in the English because we need item 8. One more page forward in the English. Under item 8 you are reporting, or rather, Cedomir Sladoje informing on your behalf that the enemy is firing from snipers, hand-held launchers, rifle-launched grenades, et cetera, in order to provoke our forces to open fire and provoke a conflict. Can you tell us these hand-held launchers and rifle-launched grenades, what calibres are these weapons and were they permitted under the terms of the agreement?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the rifle grenade is part of a rifle and it is attached to the rifle. Therefore, one might say that it could be tolerated under the agreement, not permitted but it could be tolerated because it is an integral part of a rifle. As for the hand-held launcher, its calibre is larger than 12.7 and it was impermissible to use it to fire.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You remember why the position was taken to decide that the calibre should be in excess of 12.7-millimetre. I provided one explanation but the explanation given by the Main Staff was the one that was accepted which means that every weapon in excess of 12.7-millimetres is classified as having weaponry although it does not coincide with the military classification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In line 1 it says that enemy fired on UNPROFOR helicopters and then under item 3 it says the Muslims opened fire at UN helicopters from the Sokolje sector. The helicopter was flying over our positions. What can you tell us about this and what was the purpose of firing on a helicopter while it was flying over our territory?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just like to explain in more detail the position of Sokolje. It is above Rajlovac and it is overlooking Rajlovac. Our forces were in Rajlovac whereas Sokolje was held by BH Army. The helicopter was flying -- I suppose it was following the stream of the river Bosna. I don't know where it was coming from - and then it was fired on from Sokolje. It seems to me after you've read this that I actually remember this incident, so from that area and from Vogosca and Zuc was where the fire came targeting the helicopter. Later it was established that it actually came from Sokolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, what was their objective?

utterances.speaker: STANISLAV GALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The usual one, to create a provocation and to blame the Army of Republika Srpska. If anything transpired in terms of shooting down the helicopter, we would have to prove that it wasn't our fault but I don't think that we would have had enough time to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3434, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And shall we stop here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one more document, but we can deal with it on the Monday. It's up to you. I'm in your hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll adjourn here. Mr. Galic, we'll adjourn for today and continue Monday next week at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. This will be very good for my bad back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you very much. In order for me not to be suspected of illegal activities, I think that I now have understood that on page 62, line 14, or from line 14, I have the feeling that the transcript is not very clear as opposed to what General Galic has said. I'm just making a note of it in case there might be later on questions about it. This is what I wanted to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will leave it either to Mr. Karadzic or Ms. Edgerton to take up if there's any need. Mr. Galic and Mr. Piletta-Zanin could you excuse yourselves. We have to deal with one matter in private session. Have a nice weekend.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you so much. Have a nice weekend. You too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in order not to waste too much time I will come back to the room later on to get my bags. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, shall we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just one matter, Mr. Robinson. The Chamber is seized of the motion for the temporary transfer of detained Witness Franc Kos filed on the 4th of April this year in which the accused moves for the transfer of the detained witness from Bosnia-Herzegovina to the UNDU for purposes of testimony in this -- in the Defence case. The Chamber notes that in the motion the accused submits that the two requirements for transfer pursuant to Rule 90 bis are met, namely, that the presence of the detained witness is not required for any criminal proceedings in progress in BiH and that the transfer of the witness does not extend the period of detention. However, the Chamber also notes that the accused requests the Chamber to issue an invitation to the BiH authorities to confirm these two assertions. So this is the question, whether you can clarify why the Defence team itself could not have made these inquiries prior to filing the motion and how you can affirm that requirements for Rule 90 bis are met.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That statement that was made in our motion was based upon our review of the calendar of -- or at least a review of the proceedings from the web site of the court of Bosnia-Herzegovina where it is seen that he was convicted, sentenced to 40 years in prison. So we know that the first problem is not going to be met that his sentence would be expired by the time he came here. And then we saw that there were no -- currently no appeal proceedings scheduled. So based on our review of those -- of that information, that was the basis of the representations that we made in our motion, but we thought that it was better if the Chamber wanted to satisfy itself for sure that the information be received from the Bosnian authorities. However, as I think you know, when we communicate with the Bosnian authorities absent a request from the Chamber they do not respond to us and they only act upon requests that are passed through the Chamber. So that's why we didn't contact them directly but asked the Chamber to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But you didn't contact the BiH authorities at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct. And I think you'll -- you'll remember you've urged them on several occasions in the past to co-operate. They have taken the position -- they have been very co-operative, actually, with us but only when the information is passed through the Chamber. So that's been their position and we didn't contact them directly because we assumed that they would tell us that we would have to go through the Chamber for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll continue on Monday morning. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of April, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.50 p.m.,
